title: Three Grammatical Genders and Noun Endings
subtitle: Mastering masculine, feminine, and neuter nouns along with matching adjectives
keyPoint: Marathi classifies every noun into masculine, feminine, or neuter, typically matching them with adjectives ending in -आ, -ई, and -ए respectively.

mistakes.note: Adjectives ending in variable -आ must change to -ई when modifying a feminine noun.
Unlike Hindi, 'पुस्तक' (book) in Marathi is neuter, so it takes the neuter demonstrative 'ते' rather than feminine 'ती'.
'घर' (house) is grammatically neuter in Marathi, demanding the neuter adjective ending -ए.

quiz.question: Choose the correct demonstrative pronoun for 'room' (खोली - feminine): '___ खोली मोठी आहे.'
quiz.explanation: 'खोली' is a feminine noun, so the feminine demonstrative 'ती' must be used.

quiz.question: Select the correct adjective form for 'water' (पाणी - neuter): 'इथे ___ पाणी आहे.'
quiz.explanation: 'थंड' is an invariant adjective that does not change gender suffixes, correctly modifying the neuter noun 'पाणी'.

quiz.question: Complete with the correct adjective form: 'हा ___ घोडा धावतो.' (white)
quiz.explanation: 'घोडा' is masculine singular, so the variable adjective takes the masculine suffix -आ ('पांढरा').

quiz.question: Identify the neuter phrase:
quiz.explanation: 'पान' (leaf/page) is neuter, making 'स्वच्छ पान' a neuter noun phrase.

tip: Test an unknown noun's gender using the third-person pronouns: if it pairs naturally with तो it's masculine, ती is feminine, and ते is neuter.

title: Basic Postpositions and the Oblique Case (सामान्यरूप)
subtitle: Inflecting noun stems before attaching location, motion, and associative suffixes
keyPoint: Before attaching any postposition, a Marathi noun must transform into its oblique base (सामान्यरूप).

mistakes.note: The consonant-ending neuter noun 'घर' lengthens its final syllable to '-रा' in the oblique base before suffixes like '-त'.
Feminine nouns ending in '-आ' like 'शाळा' change their ending vowel to '-ए' ('शाळे-') in the oblique case.
Masculine nouns ending in '-आ' undergo palatalization to '-या' in the oblique base.

quiz.question: Attach the postposition '-वर' (on) to 'झाड' (tree): 'पक्षी ___ बसला आहे.'
quiz.explanation: 'झाड' becomes 'झाडा-' in the oblique base before receiving '-वर'.

quiz.question: Attach '-त' (in) to 'पाणी' (water): 'मासा ___ पोहतो.'
quiz.explanation: Neuter nouns ending in '-ई' like 'पाणी' change their stem to '-यात' ('पाण्यात').

quiz.question: Complete the sentence with the oblique form of 'मुलगी' + '-ला': 'आईने ___ बोलावले.'
quiz.explanation: Feminine nouns ending in '-ई' like 'मुलगी' change stem-internal vowels to form the oblique 'मुली-' ('मुलीला').

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly demonstrates the oblique form of 'दुकान' (shop) + '-त'?
quiz.explanation: Consonant-ending neuter nouns lengthen the preceding final vowel to '-आ' ('दुकानात').

tip: Never attach a postposition like -त, -वर, or -ला directly to the base dictionary word; always check how the ending transforms into its oblique shape first.

title: Affirmative vs Negative Copula (आहे vs नाही)
subtitle: Distinguishing positive and negative existential and equational sentences
keyPoint: Use आहे for 'is/am/are' to affirm existence or identity, and substitute नाही to express negation.

mistakes.note: Do not combine 'आहे' and 'नाही' together; 'नाही' replaces 'आहे' completely in negative equational sentences.
'-स' is solely the second-person singular inflection for 'तू'; first-person 'मी' pairs with uninflected 'नाही' or 'नाहीये'.
The second-person singular pronoun 'तू' requires the specific copular agreement marker '-स' ('आहेस').

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'माझा मित्र आज इथे ___.' (is not)
quiz.explanation: 'नाही' is the standard third-person singular negative copula for present existence.

quiz.question: Choose the matching affirmative copula: 'तू खूप दयाळू ___.'
quiz.explanation: 'तू' strictly takes the second-person singular ending '-स' giving 'आहेस'.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'आम्ही सध्या पुण्यात ___.' (we are)
quiz.explanation: The first-person plural pronoun 'आम्ही' pairs with the verb form 'आहोत'.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'तिथे कोणीही पाणी ___.' (there is no water)
quiz.explanation: Negation of presence uses 'नाही'.

tip: Remember that 'नाही' inherently carries the meaning of 'is not' / 'are not' — never say 'आहे नाही' in Marathi.

title: Simple Present and Habitual Conjugation
subtitle: Expressing daily routines, universal facts, and habits with gender-number agreements
keyPoint: In the simple present habitual tense, the verb stem takes person, number, and gender endings reflecting the subject.

mistakes.note: A feminine subject ('ती') must agree with the verb using the feminine ending '-ते', not the masculine '-तो'.
Female speakers must conjugate simple present verbs with the feminine inflection '-ते'.
Plural or honorific subjects ('ते') require the plural suffix '-तात'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence for a female subject: 'सीमा दररोज शाळेत ___.' (goes)
quiz.explanation: 'सीमा' is a third-person feminine singular subject, requiring the verbal suffix '-ते' ('जाते').

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'पक्षी आकाशात उंच ___.' (birds fly, plural)
quiz.explanation: 'पक्षी' is plural here, demanding the plural verb suffix '-तात' ('उडतात').

quiz.question: Complete the sentence for a male speaker: 'मी दररोज सकाळी धावायला ___.' (I go)
quiz.explanation: A male first-person speaker uses the '-तो' inflection ('जातो').

quiz.question: Choose the correct verb for second-person masculine informal: 'तू रोज पुस्तक ___ का?' (read)
quiz.explanation: Informal 'तू' for a male addressee takes the combined suffix '-तोस'.

tip: Simple present endings follow the vowel pattern: -तो for masculine, -ते for feminine, and -तात for all plurals.

title: Imperative Forms and Politeness Registers
subtitle: Navigating intimate commands, plural requests, and respectful honorific instructions
keyPoint: Use the bare verb root for intimate commands with तू, and attach -ा or -ावे for polite and respectful requests with तुम्ही or आपण.

useCases.label: Informal / Close Command
useCases.example: तू इथे बस आणि अभ्यास कर.

mistakes.note: Using the bare stem 'बस' with elders or teachers is disrespectful; use the honorific ending '-ा' ('बसा').
'नको' is the negative imperative for informal 'तू'; polite 'तुम्ही' requires 'नका'.
Pairing informal 'तू' with polite 'बसा' causes an agreement mismatch; use bare 'बस'.

quiz.question: Politely ask an elder to drink tea: 'काका, चहा ___.'
quiz.explanation: 'प्या' is the respectful imperative form of 'पीणे' (to drink) suited for elders ('काका').

quiz.question: Form an informal negative command with 'तू': 'तू तिकडे जाऊ ___.'
quiz.explanation: 'नको' accompanies the oblique infinitive ('जाऊ') for negative commands addressing 'तू'.

quiz.question: Ask a friend informally to write down an address: 'हा पत्ता ___.'
quiz.explanation: The bare stem or short form 'लिही' is the informal imperative for 'तू'.

quiz.question: Choose the formal negative request: 'कृपया येथे गोंधळ करू ___.'
quiz.explanation: 'नका' is the polite plural negative imperative matching 'कृपया' (please).

tip: When addressing strangers, shopkeepers, or elders, always add -ा to the verb stem (or use नका for negatives) to remain naturally courteous.

title: Personal Pronouns and Politeness
subtitle: Distinguishing inclusive vs. exclusive 'we' and honorific third-person forms
keyPoint: Marathi distinguishes between inclusive 'we' (आपण) and exclusive 'we' (आम्ही), while honorific reference to an elder or respected person always requires plural pronouns and verb agreement.

useCases.label: Speaking on behalf of a separate group
useCases.example: आम्ही उद्या सकाळी पुण्याला निघणार आहोत.

useCases.label: Showing respect to elders or teachers

mistakes.note: Using the singular 'तो' for a grandfather or elder is disrespectful; use the honorific plural 'ते'.
When asking someone to join you together, use the inclusive 'आपण', not exclusive 'आम्ही'.
The polite pronoun 'तुम्ही' requires the plural verb inflection '-ता', not the informal '-तोस'.

quiz.question: Choose the inclusive 'we' to invite the listener: '___ will have dinner together.'
quiz.explanation: 'आपण' includes the speaker and the listener together.

quiz.question: Select the correct honorific pronoun: '___ are my respected father.'
quiz.explanation: 'ते' is the masculine honorific plural pronoun used to address or refer to elders politely.

quiz.question: To inform a listener that 'we (not you)' are traveling, choose: '___ are going to Mumbai.'
quiz.explanation: 'आम्ही' is the exclusive first-person plural, excluding the listener.

quiz.question: Pick the correct polite verb form for 'तुम्ही कुठे ___?' (Where are you going?)
quiz.explanation: The respectful 2nd-person pronoun 'तुम्ही' requires the plural suffix '-ता'.

tip: Think of आपण as 'you + I together', whereas आम्ही is 'someone else + I (without you)'.

title: Split Ergativity in the Past Tense
subtitle: Marking transitive agents with instrumental suffixes while agreeing with the object
keyPoint: In the Marathi past tense of transitive verbs, the subject takes an instrumental marker (-ने, -नी) and the verb agrees with the direct object in gender and number.

useCases.label: Singular masculine agent acting on a feminine object
useCases.example: त्याने काल एक नवी गाडी घेतली.

useCases.label: Plural agent acting on a neuter plural object
Feminine agent acting on a masculine object

mistakes.note: In the transitive past tense, the verb agrees with the neuter object 'सफरचंद' (खाल्ले), not with the speaker 'मी'.
The subject must take the instrumental marker '-ने' (आईने), and the verb must agree with masculine 'चहा' (बनवला).
'पत्र' is neuter singular in Marathi, so the verb must end in '-ले' (लिहिले).

quiz.question: Choose the correct past verb form: 'मुलाने पेढा ___.' (The boy ate a pedha [masculine]).
quiz.explanation: 'पेढा' is masculine singular, so the past transitive verb must be 'खाल्ला'.

quiz.question: Fill in the agent marker: 'राधा___ छान गाणे गायले.' (Radha sang a nice song).
quiz.explanation: Transitive past subjects take the instrumental suffix '-ने' (राधा + ने = राधाने).

quiz.question: Identify the proper verb agreement: 'आम्ही तीन पुस्तके ___.' (We read three books [neuter plural]).
quiz.explanation: Neuter plural objects ('पुस्तके') trigger the '-ली' ending on past transitive verbs ('वाचली').

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'शिक्षकांनी मुलांना प्रश्न ___.' (The teacher asked a question [masculine]).
quiz.explanation: The direct object 'प्रश्न' is masculine singular, requiring 'विचारला'.

tip: Always identify the grammatical gender and number of the DIRECT OBJECT first; that tells you exactly how the transitive past verb must end.

title: Intransitive Past Tense Conjugation
subtitle: Conjugating verbs without direct objects to match the subject directly
keyPoint: Unlike transitive verbs, intransitive past verbs require an unmarked subject in the nominative case and agree directly with that subject in person, gender, and number.

mistakes.note: Intransitive verbs do NOT take the ergative/instrumental marker '-ने'. The subject stays nominative 'तो'.
The feminine singular subject 'ती' requires the feminine past agreement ending '-ली'.
'-स' is for 2nd person singular ('तू'). First person plural with 'आम्ही' takes '-लो'.

quiz.question: Complete the intransitive sentence: 'ती मुलगी जोरात ___.' (That girl ran [feminine]).
quiz.explanation: 'मुलगी' is feminine singular, so the intransitive past verb ends in '-ली' (धावली).

quiz.question: Choose the correct form for a male speaker: 'मी गावाहून ___.' (I arrived/came).
quiz.explanation: A 1st-person masculine singular subject 'मी' takes the ending '-लो' (आलो).

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'पक्षी आकाशात ___.' (The birds flew [masculine plural]).
quiz.explanation: 'पक्षी' here is masculine plural, requiring the agreement '-ले' (उडाले).

quiz.question: Select the correct sentence with proper subject casing:
quiz.explanation: Intransitive verbs keep the subject in the unmarked nominative form ('मुलगा').

tip: Verbs of motion (जाणे, येणे, पळणे, निघणे) and states (झोपणे, बसणे, उठणे) are intransitive; never put '-ने' on their subjects!

title: Dative Subject Constructions
subtitle: Expressing internal states, obligations, and needs using the -ला marker
keyPoint: In Marathi experiencer constructions expressing feelings, illness, needs (पाहिजे), or obligations, the logical subject takes the dative suffix '-ला' while the verb or modal reflects the experienced thing.

useCases.label: Expressing physical sensation or illness
useCases.example: मला आज खूप भूक लागली आहे.

useCases.label: Expressing necessity or desire with पाहिजे
Expressing liking or taste with आवडणे

mistakes.note: Needs expressed with 'पाहिजे' require the dative subject 'मला', never the nominative 'मी'.
The experiencer of liking must take the dative marker '-ला' (त्याला).
The verb 'आवडतात' must agree in plural number with the liked items ('आंबे' - mangoes).

quiz.question: Select the correct pronoun: '___ चहा पाहिजे.' (I want tea).
quiz.explanation: 'पाहिजे' governs the dative experiencer case, so 'मला' (to me) is required.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'सुरेशला क्रिकेट ___.' (Suresh likes cricket [masculine]).
quiz.explanation: 'क्रिकेट' is treated as masculine singular here, so the verb is 'आवडतो'.

quiz.question: Choose the right experiencer form: '___ खूप तहान लागली आहे.' (She is very thirsty).
quiz.explanation: Involuntary bodily states take the dative case; feminine 3rd person singular becomes 'तिला'.

quiz.question: Pick the right form for 'We understand this': 'आम्हाला हे ___.'
quiz.explanation: The pronoun 'हे' (this thing, neuter singular) governs the verb ending '-ते' (समजते).

tip: Whenever expressing 'want' (पाहिजे), 'like' (आवडणे), or bodily urges (भूक/तहान लागणे), immediately affix '-ला' to the person feeling it.

title: Present Continuous Tense
subtitle: Constructing ongoing actions with imperfective participles and आहे
keyPoint: The present continuous tense is formed by adding the invariable suffix '-त' to the verb stem, followed by the present tense auxiliary 'आहे' conjugated for subject gender, number, and person.

useCases.label: Action occurring at the exact moment of speech
Temporary ongoing situation or activity
useCases.example: मी सध्या एका प्रकल्पावर काम करत आहे.

mistakes.note: Use the invariable participle ending in '-त' (करत), not the habitual form 'करतो', for continuous actions.
The auxiliary verb must agree with 1st person plural 'आम्ही' by using 'आहोत'.
Singular non-honorific feminine 'ती' requires the singular auxiliary 'आहे', not plural 'आहेत'.

quiz.question: Form the present continuous: 'आम्ही जेवण ___.' (We are eating food).
quiz.explanation: Stem 'जेव' + '-त' plus the 1st person plural auxiliary 'आहोत' creates 'जेवत आहोत'.

quiz.question: Choose the right participle ending: 'मुलगा वेगाने धाव___ आहे.' (The boy is running fast).
quiz.explanation: The present continuous stem always receives the invariant suffix '-त' (धावत).

quiz.question: Select the correct auxiliary for 'तू': 'तू काय लिहीत ___?' (What are you writing?)
quiz.explanation: The 2nd person informal singular pronoun 'तू' pairs with 'आहेस'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence honorifically: 'गुरुजी फळ्यावर लिहीत ___.' (The teacher is writing on the board).
quiz.explanation: Respected subjects like 'गुरुजी' require the honorific plural auxiliary 'आहेत'.

tip: The continuous marker '-त' never changes for gender or number; only the ending auxiliary (आहे, आहेस, आहोत, आहेत) changes to match the subject!

title: Future Tense Formation and Agreement
subtitle: Adding personal endings directly to verb stems to talk about tomorrow
keyPoint: Marathi forms the simple future tense by appending synthetic person-number suffixes directly to the raw verb stem.

useCases.label: Polite Queries & Promises
useCases.example: आम्ही तुमचे काम वेळेवर पूर्ण करू.

examples.en: तो आज रात्री उशिरा घरी येईल.
सर्व मुले उद्या मैदानावर क्रिकेट खेळतील.

mistakes.note: The suffix -ईल/-एल is strictly for third-person singular (he/she/it); first-person 'I' requires -ईन.
Second-person informal 'तू' must take -शील, not third-person -ईल.
Third-person plural requires the suffix -तील, whereas -ईन is reserved for first-person singular.

quiz.question: I will drink tea tomorrow: 'मी उद्या चहा _____.'
quiz.explanation: First-person singular 'मी' takes the future suffix -ईन, turning root पि- into पिईन.

quiz.question: Will you (informal) come with us?: 'तू आमच्यासोबत _____ का?'
quiz.explanation: The informal second-person pronoun 'तू' pairs with the suffix -शील.

quiz.question: She will write a letter: 'ती पत्र _____.'
quiz.explanation: Third-person singular feminine 'ती' uses the future ending -ईल.

quiz.question: They will play football: 'ते फुटबॉल _____.'
quiz.explanation: Third-person plural 'ते' requires the suffix -तील.

tip: Unlike Hindi which adds separate inflected markers like 'गा/गे/गी', Marathi integrates the tense ending directly onto the verb root like Romance languages.

title: Potential and Permission Modals (शकणे vs मिळणे)
subtitle: Distinguishing internal capability from external permission and opportunity
keyPoint: Use roots + शकणे for direct personal ability, but pair the dative subject with an infinitive + मिळणे for permission or opportunity.

cells: मला बोलू द्या / मला बोलायला मिळाले.
I got the chance to speak.

useCases.label: Inherent Physical Capacity
useCases.example: तो एवढे जड वजन सहज उचलू शकतो.

examples.en: तू हे कठीण गणित सोडवू शकतोस का?
आम्ही आज वेळेवर पोहोचू शकलो नाही.
मला काल चित्रपट पाहायला मिळाला नाही.

mistakes.note: When asking direct personal ability or permission without dative casing, use the potential verb शकणे.
The verb शकणे takes a standard nominative subject (मी), not a dative subject (मला).
For having the opportunity or fortune to go, Marathi uses dative + मिळणे rather than शकणे.

quiz.question: Can you lift this bag?: 'तू ही पिशवी उचलू _____ का?'
quiz.explanation: Direct capacity with nominative 'तू' demands the modal verb शकणे in 2nd person: शकतोस.

quiz.question: I got an opportunity to watch the match: 'मला सामना _____ मिळाला.'
quiz.explanation: The verb मिळणे governs an oblique/purposive infinitive ending in -यला (पाहायला).

quiz.question: She cannot come today: 'ती आज येऊ _____ नाही.'
quiz.explanation: In negative present potentiality, शकणे takes its invariant participle stem शकत.

quiz.question: We did not get permission/a chance to enter: 'आम्हाला आत जायला _____ नाही.'
quiz.explanation: Opportunity with dative subject 'आम्हाला' uses negative past of मिळणे: मिळाले नाही.

tip: Remember: शकणे = 'I am able' (nominative subject); मिळणे = 'Opportunity was received by me' (dative subject: मला, तुला, त्याला).

title: Causative Verb Morphology (प्रयोजक क्रियापदे)
subtitle: Transforming base verbs into transitive and causative actions using infixes
keyPoint: Marathi creates causative verbs systematically by adding the infix -व- (-वि-) before the infinitive marker, turning 'to do' into 'to cause to do'.

examples.en: त्या विनोदी नाटकाने आम्हांला खूप हसवले.

mistakes.note: करणे means simply 'to do/make'; causing an agent to eat requires the causative root भरवणे or जेवू घालणे.
हसणे is intransitive (to laugh). Making another laugh requires transitive causative हसवणे with neuter agreement in the past.
Causative and transitive perfective verbs must take ergative agent marking (-ने) on the subject.

quiz.question: The joker makes everyone laugh: 'विदूषक सर्वांना _____.'
quiz.explanation: The causative form of हसणे (to laugh) is हसवणे, conjugate for present tense: हसवतो.

quiz.question: Mother puts the baby to sleep: 'आई बाळाला _____.'
quiz.explanation: The causative form of झोपणे (to sleep) is झोपवणे (to put to sleep).

quiz.question: He got the letter written by his assistant: 'त्याने साहाय्यकाकडून पत्र _____ घेतले.'
quiz.explanation: The causative conjunctive participle form is लिहवून (having caused to write).

quiz.question: The trainer made the horse run: 'प्रशिक्षकाने घोड्याला _____.'
quiz.explanation: The causative of पळणे (to run) is पळवणे, which takes neuter past ending -ले with dative object.

tip: When deriving causatives, short stem vowels frequently undergo strengthening or simply insert the -व- suffix: बसणे → बसवणे, शिकणे → शिकवणे (to learn → to teach).

title: Conjunctive Participle (-ऊन Suffix)
subtitle: Connecting chronological actions smoothly into one fluid sentence
keyPoint: Add the suffix -ऊन to any verb root to signify 'having done X', joining consecutive actions sharing identical subjects without conjunctions.

useCases.label: Cause Preceding Effect
useCases.example: तो बातमी ऐकून खूप आनंदी झाला.

examples.en: आम्ही चहा पिऊन कामाला सुरुवात केली.
तो गृहपाठ संपवून मैदानावर खेळायला गेला.
आई बाजारात जाऊन भाजीपाला घेऊन आली.
तिने शांतपणे विचार करून योग्य निर्णय घेतला.

mistakes.wrong: मी जेवण केले आणि मी झोपलो.
mistakes.note: While 'आणि' is understood, native Marathi natural speech chains consecutive same-subject verbs using the -ऊन participle.
Use the conjunctive stem धावून instead of mixing unmatched finite verb tenses across clauses.
Do not use -ऊन when the two clauses have distinct subjects (पाऊस vs मी); use causal subordinators like -मुळे instead.

quiz.question: Wash your hands and eat food: 'हात _____ जेवायला बस.'
quiz.explanation: The conjunctive participle of धुणे (to wash) is formed by adding -ऊन: धुवून.

quiz.question: Having heard the news, she wept: 'बातमी _____ ती रडू लागली.'
quiz.explanation: Root ऐक- plus suffix -ऊन yields ऐकून ('having heard').

quiz.question: Finish your work and go home: 'काम _____ घरी जा.'
quiz.explanation: The irregular conjunctive participle of करणे is करून.

quiz.question: Having arrived at the station, we called him: 'आम्ही स्थानकावर _____ त्याला फोन केला.'
quiz.explanation: Root पोहोच- plus conjunctive suffix -ऊन yields पोहोचून.

tip: Verb stems ending in vowels often undergo glide insertions or contractions: करणे becomes करून, and धुणे becomes धुवून.

title: Necessity and Obligation (-आवे लागते / -ायचे आहे)
subtitle: Differentiating external compulsion from personal duties and intentions
keyPoint: Use the potential stem + लागणे for inescapable external compulsion, and the verbal noun (-ायचे) + असणे for personal plans or duties.

cells: Personal plan, duty, or strong desire
Ethical duty, advice, or polite mandate

useCases.label: Personal Daily Objective
useCases.example: मला आज संध्याकाळी किराणा आणायचा आहे.

examples.en: मला दररोज सकाळी पाच वाजता उठावे लागते.
त्याला आज तातडीने पुणे गाठावे लागले.
मला हे पुस्तक दोन दिवसांत वाचायचे आहे.
आम्हाला नवीन घर विकत घ्यायचे आहे.

mistakes.note: Impersonal obligative constructions with लागणे require the subject in the dative case (मला, not मी).
The verb preceding लागणे must end in -आवे agreement markers (-आवा/-आवी/-आवे), matching the gender/number of the object.
Do not blend पाहिजे with आहे; personal intention uses the -ायचे आहे construction directly.

quiz.question: I have to wake up early every day (compulsion): 'मला दररोज लवकर _____.'
quiz.explanation: Routine external necessity uses the dative subject + -आवे लागते construction.

quiz.question: I want/plan to buy a new laptop: 'मला नवीन लॅपटॉप _____.'
quiz.explanation: A masculine object (लॅपटॉप) pairs with personal desiderative marker -आयचा आहे (घ्यायचा आहे).

quiz.question: He had to pay a fine yesterday: 'त्याला काल दंड _____.'
quiz.explanation: Past external obligation for masculine object 'दंड' requires भरावा लागला.

quiz.question: You ought to tell the truth: 'तुम्ही सत्य _____.'
quiz.explanation: Moral propriety or polite imperative takes the -आवे subjunctive suffix (बोलावे).

tip: Pay attention to gender agreement! In 'मला आंबा खायचा आहे' vs 'मला पोळी खायची आहे', the -ायचे suffix shifts to -आयचा (masc.) or -आयची (fem.) to match the object.

title: Relative-Correlative Syntax (जो... तो / जे... ते)
subtitle: Linking relative conditions and descriptions with correlative pronouns
keyPoint: Marathi relative clauses introduce an entity with a 'ज-' pronoun and resolve it in the main clause with a matching 'त-' correlative pronoun.

cells: जो अभ्यास करतो, तो उत्तीर्ण होतो.
जी मुलगी धावते, ती माझी बहीण आहे.
जे चकाकते, ते सर्व सोने नसते.
ज्या गाड्या निघाल्या, त्या वेळेवर पोहोचल्या.

useCases.label: Identifying People
useCases.example: जो माणूस काल आला होता, तो डॉक्टर आहे.

examples.en: जो मेहनत करतो, तो नक्की यशस्वी होतो.
जी गाडी पहिली येईल, ती आपल्याला मिळेल.
जे सत्य असते, ते कधी लपत नाही.
ज्यांनी मदत केली, त्यांचे आभार माना.
जिथे शांतता असते, तिथे सुख नांदते.

mistakes.wrong: जो मुलगी गाते, तो छान आहे.
mistakes.right: जी मुलगी गाते, ती छान आहे.
mistakes.note: Relative pronouns must match the gender of the noun; मुलगी is feminine and takes जी... ती.

mistakes.wrong: जे काम तू केले, तो चांगले आहे.
mistakes.right: जे काम तू केले, ते चांगले आहे.
mistakes.note: काम is neuter, so both the relative and correlative must match in neuter: जे... ते.

mistakes.wrong: जो अभ्यास करतो, आणि तो पास होतो.
mistakes.right: जो अभ्यास करतो, तो पास होतो.
mistakes.note: Do not insert आणि between the relative clause and the correlative clause.

quiz.question: Complete the maxim: 'All that glitters is not gold.' -> ___ चकाकते, ते सोने नसते.
quiz.explanation: The neuter pronoun जे matches the correlative pronoun ते.

quiz.question: Complete the pair: 'He who works hard succeeds.' -> ___ कष्ट करतो, तो पुढे जातो.
quiz.explanation: The correlative तो is masculine singular, so it pairs with masculine relative जो.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'The girl who ran fast won.' -> ___ मुलगी जोरात धावली, ती जिंकली.
quiz.explanation: मुलगी is feminine singular, requiring the feminine relative pronoun जी.

quiz.question: Match the adverbial relative: 'Where there is water, there is life.' -> जिथे पाणी असते, ___ जीवन असते.
quiz.explanation: The spatial relative adverb जिथे ('where') pairs with correlative तिथे ('there').

tip: Remember the golden rule of Marathi syntax: ज- words set up the clause, and त- words complete the thought.

title: Compound Verbs with Aspectual Auxiliaries (टाकणे, देणे, घेणे)
subtitle: Using vector auxiliaries to specify completeness, direction, and attitude
keyPoint: A compound verb joins a conjunctive stem ending in -ऊन with a vector auxiliary to add nuance like suddenness, self-benefit, or other-directed action.

useCases.label: Self-Directed Activity
useCases.example: मी माझे कपडे इस्त्री करून घेतले.

examples.en: मी ही नवी भाषा शिकून घेतली.
तो मुलगा धावताना खाली पडून गेला.
तिने सर्व जुनी पुस्तके विकून टाकली.

mistakes.note: Actions done for one's own benefit require घेणे (करून घेतला), while देणे implies benefiting someone else.
The primary verb must take the conjunctive participle form ending in -ऊन (फाडून), not the infinitive.
Involuntary intransitive processes take संपून with जाणे, not the causative संपवून.

quiz.question: Choose the vector verb indicating self-benefit: 'I understood the lesson (for myself).' -> मी धडा समजून ___.
quiz.explanation: घेणे indicates an inward action performed for the subject's own comprehension or benefit.

quiz.question: Express decisive completion/riddance: 'He tore up the letter.' -> त्याने पत्र फाडून ___.
quiz.explanation: टाकणे conveys decisive, irreversible completion and disposal.

quiz.question: Indicate an action done to help someone else: 'She explained the problem to her friend.' -> तिने मैत्रिणीला प्रश्न समजावून ___.
quiz.explanation: देणे expresses an action directed outward for the benefit of another person.

quiz.question: Express unintentional change of state: 'The cat drank up all the milk and ran away.' -> मांजर दूध पिऊन ___.
quiz.explanation: निघून जाणे / पिऊन जाणे uses जाणे to depict complete departure or final state transition.

tip: To choose between देणे and घेणे, ask: 'Who is the receiver of the benefit?' If it flows outward to another, use देणे; if inward to oneself, use घेणे.

title: Neuter Impersonal Construction (भावे प्रयोग)
subtitle: When neither subject nor object controls the verb
keyPoint: When both subject and direct object carry postpositional markers, the verb is frozen in the third-person neuter singular ending (-ले).

cells: I am able to walk now

mistakes.note: Because the direct object has the marker -ला, the verb cannot agree with it and must end in neuter singular -ले.
Even though Sita is feminine, the marker -ला blocks feminine agreement on the verb.
Do not add plural agreement suffixes to impersonal verbs; keep the strict 3rd-person neuter singular -ले.

quiz.question: Choose the correct verb form: शिक्षकांनी सर्व मुलांना वर्गात ___.
quiz.explanation: Both subject and object take case markers, so the verb defaults strictly to third-person neuter singular ending in -ले.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence correctly: मांजराने उंदराला शेवटी ___.
quiz.explanation: The object उंदीर takes the accusative marker -ला, preventing agreement and triggering the neuter form पकडले.

quiz.question: Identify the correct form: पोलिसांनी त्या आरोपीला ताबडतोब ___.
quiz.explanation: The impersonal causal verb takes the neutral -ले ending when the object carries -ला.

quiz.question: Which sentence demonstrates proper Bhave Prayog (भावे प्रयोग)?
quiz.explanation: Both Radha (-ने) and Meera (-ला) have markers, yielding the invariant neuter verb पाहिले.

tip: If you see -ने on the subject AND -ला on the object, the verb suffix is virtually guaranteed to end with neuter -ले.

title: Irrealis Conditionals (संकेतार्थ -ता / -ते)
subtitle: Expressing hypothetical, unrealized conditions and counterfactual pasts
keyPoint: Unreal conditionals pair hypothetical condition and consequence clauses using habitual past suffixes (-ता, -ती, -ते, -तो) across both verbs.

useCases.label: Past Counterfactual Consequence
useCases.example: तू अभ्यास केला असतास तर उत्तीर्ण झाला असतास.

useCases.label: Hypothetical Present/Future Wish
useCases.example: पाऊस पडला तर शेतकरी आनंदी होतील.

useCases.label: Unrealized Opportunity in the Past
useCases.example: गाडी वेळेवर आली असती तर आम्ही पोहोचलो असतो.

examples.en: तू वेळेवर आला असतास तर आपण भेटलो असतो.
चांगला पाऊस पडता तर पिके छान आली असती.
मी तिथे असतो तर त्याला नक्की मदत केली असती.
पैसे असते तर मी नवीन घर विकत घेतले असते.
तिने औषध घेतले असते तर ती बरी झाली असती.

mistakes.right: तू आला असतास तर मी गेलो असतो.
mistakes.note: Counterfactual past conditions require the conditional auxiliary असता paired with the conditional verb form.

mistakes.wrong: ती आली असती तर काम झाले असता.
mistakes.right: ती आली असती तर काम झाले असते.
mistakes.note: The neuter subject काम requires the neuter auxiliary असते, not masculine असता.

mistakes.wrong: आम्ही अभ्यास केला तर पास झालो असतो.
mistakes.right: आम्ही अभ्यास केला असता तर पास झालो असतो.
mistakes.note: Both clauses in counterfactual past sentences must reflect the irrealis conditional morphology.

quiz.question: Complete the counterfactual sentence: जर पाऊस पडला असता, तर धरण ___.
quiz.explanation: The protasis is past counterfactual, so the neuter noun धरण takes the auxiliary clause भरले असते.

quiz.question: Select the correct second-person masculine form: जर तू बोलावले असतेस, तर मी नक्की ___.
quiz.explanation: A counterfactual statement by a masculine speaker takes the habitual past auxiliary आलो असतो.

quiz.question: Choose the grammatically matching form: ती मुलगी इथे असती तर तिने गाणे ___.
quiz.explanation: The verb agrees with the neuter noun गाणे in transitive perfective, resulting in म्हटले असते.

quiz.question: Which conjunction pair correctly frames this conditional?
quiz.explanation: Irrealis conditional statements are standardly constructed using the correlative pair जर ... तर.

tip: Remember to match the gender and number of the auxiliary असता/असती/असते to the controlling noun of each respective clause.

title: Passive and Incapacitative Voice (कर्मणी and शक्य प्रयोग)
subtitle: Passive constructions with जाणे and physiological capacity markers
keyPoint: Formal passive voice uses the past participle with auxiliary जाणे, while physiological ability or inability inflects the verbal root with -व-.

useCases.label: Physiological / Inherent Inability
useCases.example: तब्बेत बरी नसल्यामुळे त्याला जेवत नाही.

examples.en: पाय दुखत असल्याने मला डोंगर चढवत नाही.
शहरात नवीन पूल बांधला जात आहे.

mistakes.wrong: मी हे काम केले जात आहे.
mistakes.right: माझ्याकडून हे काम केले जात आहे.
mistakes.note: In passive sentences with जाणे, the human agent must be marked by कडून, not simple nominative pronoun मी.
The incapacitative construction requires the potential stem infix -व- (चालवत नाही, not चालत नाही).
Since पत्र is neuter singular, the participle and auxiliary verb must both agree in neuter form: लिहिले गेले.

quiz.question: Choose the correct analytical passive: 'The bridge was built by the government.'
quiz.explanation: The analytical passive uses the agentive marker कडून alongside the auxiliary form बांधला गेला.

quiz.question: Express incapacitative inability: 'Due to weakness, she cannot walk.'
quiz.explanation: Physiological involuntary incapacity is expressed via the instrumental or dative subject with the -वत stem: तिच्याने चालवत नाही.

quiz.question: Select the correct neuter plural passive ending: सर्व पुस्तके काल ग्रंथालयात ___.
quiz.explanation: पुस्तके is neuter plural; the past participle and passive auxiliary take the neuter plural -ली ending (जमा केली गेली).

quiz.question: Select the appropriate capacity verb form: ताप कमी झाल्यावर आता त्याला थोडेफार ___.
quiz.explanation: The potential stem adds infix -व-, resulting in जेववते when indicating acquired physical capacity.

tip: Distinguish between modal impossibility (शकत नाही - mental or external barrier) and incapacitative voice (-वत नाही - internal physical barrier).
